title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.80): K is a number field, Γ = Gal(K̄/K), and X/K is an anabelian curve (hyperbolic, possibly affine). A rational point x is attached to a Galois-invariant étale path class from x0 to x. This gives a class f_{x0,x} in H^1(Γ, π̂_1(X,x0)), and for a single path ℓ: x0→x a 1-cocycle f_ℓ: Γ → π̂_1(x0). The injectivity half of the section conjecture says x is determined by this class. Grothendieck then asks for an 'explicit determination' of f_ℓ(u) for u ∈ Γ.

Since Γ itself is not explicitly known, he proposes to locate (repérer) u by 'coordinates': the images g^α_{x,y}(u) ∈ Π̂_α of finitely many generating arrows of reference fundamental groupoids Π_1(X_α, I_α), for α ∈ A and base points x, y ∈ I_α. On the next page the most natural reference variety is U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞}, with its base points.

The hope expressed on this page is for 'explicit formulas'. These would depend on precise arithmetic properties of the particular point x, and on its characteristic invariants in the Mordell–Weil–Néron situation (Mordell–Weil group, Néron models or heights). They would express f_ℓ(u) in terms of the coordinates of u. He calls this 'a fascinating work in perspective, which I have practically not started yet'.

He then observes that the proof of uniqueness via Mordell–Weil shows more: x is already determined by the abelianized class (34), (f_{x0,x})_ab ∈ H^1(Γ, π̂_1(X,x0)^ab). In modern terms this is the Kummer class of the divisor class x − x0 in H^1(Γ, T̂J), where J is the (generalized) Jacobian, a semiabelian variety. Injectivity follows from three facts:
- the Abel–Jacobi map is injective;
- J(K) is finitely generated (Mordell–Weil, plus Dirichlet for the torus part), so J(K) → J(K)^ is injective;
- the Kummer map J(K)^ → H^1(Γ, T̂J) is injective.

Hence it suffices to find explicit formulas for the abelianized cocycles (f_ℓ)_ab. The question is thereby reduced to the same question with X replaced by an abelian variety, or an extension of one by a torus (a generalized Jacobian).

The next page notes the catch: Γ does not act faithfully on π_1 of such a variety. So the coordinates of u must come essentially from other varieties, above all U_{0,3}. The programme is therefore to express Kummer classes of points of semiabelian varieties in terms of the Galois action on π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}).
errors: No mathematical error, but there is a gap for genus 0. For an affine X of genus 0 the uniqueness argument relies on finite generation of S-units (Dirichlet) rather than Mordell–Weil. This is presumably implicit in 'Mordell-Weil-Néron' and in the generalized Jacobian.
The 'explicit formulas' are a hoped-for programme only. Nothing is proven or formulated precisely on this page.
For G_m the formula is trivially explicit: Kummer characters u ↦ u(a^{1/n})/a^{1/n}. The real content lies in expressing these via the U_{0,3} coordinates of u, which is not addressed here.

ideas.what: Injectivity of the section map for curves follows from Mordell–Weil via the abelianized (Kummer) class; the class in H^1(Γ, π_1^ab) already determines the point
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity part of the section conjecture via the Kummer map on the (generalized) Jacobian
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings, 1983); standard in Stix's 'Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups'
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (27 June 1983), as I recall; it states injectivity is an easy consequence of Mordell–Weil — unsure of exact wording

ideas.what: Locating a Galois element u by its action on finitely many generating arrows of reference fundamental groupoids (Π_1(X_α, I_α) with chosen base points)
ideas.modern_name: Coordinates of Galois elements via their action on fundamental groupoids with tangential base points (Ihara/Drinfeld–GT style parametrization)

ideas.what: Programme: explicit formulas for the Galois cocycle of a rational point (path x0→x) in terms of arithmetic invariants of x and the coordinates of u, reduced to semiabelian varieties and expressed via U_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: Explicit formulas for ℓ-adic Galois polylogarithms / Kummer properties of Galois action on paths; explicit Kummer classes for elliptic curves via Galois action on π_1 of the projective line minus three points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Anderson–Ihara, Nakamura (explicit formulae, elliptic case), Wojtkowiak (ℓ-adic polylogarithms and iterated integrals), Nakamura–Wojtkowiak

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets as an explicit research programme the task of writing the cocycle f_ℓ(u) of a rational point as a formula. The formula should use arithmetic invariants of x (Mordell–Weil/Néron data) and the 'coordinates' of u given by its action on reference groupoids such as π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}). Via abelianization he reduces the problem to Kummer classes on semiabelian varieties. Pieces were later done independently: Wojtkowiak's ℓ-adic polylogarithms and Nakamura's explicit formulas in the elliptic and once-punctured-elliptic cases. A general programme of 'explicit section/Kummer classes in GT coordinates', tied to Néron-height-type invariants, does not seem to have been carried out systematically.
missed.quote: on peut espérer donner des "formules" explicites, dépendant sur des propriétés arithmétiques précises des points particuliers x ... qui donnent f_ℓ(u) en termes des paramètres précédents fixant u. C'est là un travail fascinant en perspective
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The idea of expressing Kummer classes of rational points of abelian varieties through the GT/U_{0,3} action is close to work on elliptic Galois polylogarithms and Chabauty–Kim style explicit computations. As a unified programme it remains largely open and could interest people working on explicit anabelian methods.

deep.surprise_reason: The injectivity-via-Mordell–Weil remark is known and was communicated by Grothendieck himself. The explicit-formula programme anticipates later work by Ihara, Nakamura and Wojtkowiak, and the link to Néron/arithmetic invariants is only gestured at. It is a documented early vision, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'ou de façon équivalente, par les g^α_{x,y}(u) ∈ Π̂_α', not 'en des façons équivalentes'.
'Ceci suffit;' is more likely 'Ceci posé;' or 'Ceci précisé,'.
'qui donnent f_e(x)' should read 'qui donnent f_ℓ(u)'.
'H^1(Γ, Π̂_1(∞))' should read 'H^1(Γ, π̂_1(x_0))' (equivalently π̂_1(X, x_0)).
'remplaçant X par une VA ou cat. d'icelles' should read 'ou ext. d'icelles' (an extension of an abelian variety by a torus), continuing 'par un tore' on the next page.
'(dans la situation Mordell-Weil-Néron)' is correctly read.
The margin note seems to begin 'C'est une question particulière, mais plus intéressante en fait...'; the rest is uncertain.
